problem: The CMU VLA Challenge needs an agent that explores an unseen indoor scene and answers numerical, object-reference and instruction-following queries within 10 minutes. Memoryless VLMs (e.g. BLIP2 on the current frame) and random exploration with text-file memory fail, and scene-graph pipelines like VLA-3D assume a pre-built 3D model.
motivation: Real robots have no pre-supplied 3D model, so the agent must build its own structured, queryable world model online under a strict time budget. The observation that drives the design is that VLMs answer spatial and numerical questions well when given structured map context, and that the exploration and mapping time is the main bottleneck.
key_idea: Build a time-limited semantic voxel map of OwlViT embeddings during full-coverage exploration, then use Gemini to classify the query, ground the object nouns in the map and generate a context-rich prompt whose answer is converted into a marker, a count or waypoints.
insight: Structured persistent memory was the pivotal step: the BLIP2 single-frame approach and random exploration with a text-file memory failed. Practical tuning matters under a time limit: larger waypoint spacing (0.6 to 1.25 m), a relaxed arrival threshold (0.65 to 1.0 m) and a larger voxel size (0.15 m) cut exploration from 8m42s to 4m17s, reportedly without hurting QA accuracy. No quantitative ablation of accuracy is provided.
method: Autonomous exploration: builds a 2D grid map from LiDAR, samples traversable points with a minimum spacing and a distance-transform safety buffer, computes a tour over them, and a waypoint controller executes it.

Semantic voxel map: OwlViT (owlvit-base-patch32) embeddings of detected objects, with 3D coordinates and scale, are integrated iteratively into a voxel map. Exploration is capped at 500 s, after which the partial map is used.
Query classification: Gemini 2.0 Flash classifies the instruction as numerical, object reference or instruction-following.
Object grounding: the VLM extracts key nouns, and the text embedding of each noun is matched by similarity against the voxel-map embeddings to retrieve 3D points.
Contextual prompt generation: object names, 3D coordinates, scale and 2D grid locations are formatted into a prompt for Gemini, with DeepSeek V3 as a fallback API.

Post-processing/action generation: parses an integer for counts, publishes an RViz marker for object references, and for instruction-following parses plans such as Goto and Avoidbetween, edits the grid, plans a path and executes it via the waypoint controller.
Time optimizations: sparser waypoints, a relaxed arrival threshold and a larger voxel size.

setting.backbone: Gemini 2.0 Flash (frozen, DeepSeek V3 fallback) + OwlViT base-patch32 (frozen) for embeddings
setting.action_space: waypoints executed by a ROS waypoint controller on a 2D grid map
setting.simulator: CMU VLA Challenge Unity simulator (Habitat/Matterport3D-based scenes)

numbers_note: No quantitative task metrics are reported; only qualitative example answers and exploration time (8m42s to 4m17s).
results: The system is demonstrated on one office scene of the challenge with example answers (e.g. 12 chairs; coordinates for a potted plant and a paper cup). Optimizations reduced exploration time from 8m42s to 4m17s (about 50%). No benchmark scores or baseline comparisons are given.
limitations: Relies on online VLM APIs (latency, network dependence).
Assumes a static environment with a sequential explore-then-act pipeline.
Evaluated qualitatively on a single scene, with no quantitative accuracy or baseline comparison.
